text:
leigh: Opening a focused PR to clarify Dedicated isolation semantics and add a migration appendix for Private deployments. Goal: one page for isolation behaviors (eviction vs preemption vs tenant-affinity), one page with migration recipes, and a tiny Go SDK snippet for pool config. Draft: https://github.com/redwood/inference-docs/pull/4991

priya: I'll own the Go SDK example and a short code comment explaining how tenant affinity influences routing. Planning to show both strict and best-effort examples.

samir: Important to call out that eviction can happen after graceful drain window expires. Suggest a timeline diagram and an explicit example for fallback routing: add `fallback_model: \"rw-small-quant\"` and `retry_policy: { attempts: 1, backoff_ms: 250 }`.

priya: Prototype Go snippet (WIP):
```go
client := redwood.NewClient(REDWOOD_KEY)
pool, err := client.CreateDedicatedPool(ctx, redwood.DedicatedPoolConfig{
    Name: \"team-b\",
    ReservedGPUs: 2,
    Autoscale: redwood.Autoscale{Min:1, Max:6, Metric: \"p95_latency_ms\", Target:200},
    Isolation: redwood.Isolation{TenantAffinity: \"strict\", Preemptible: false},
})
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
fmt.Println(\"created pool\", pool.ID)
```

tomas: For the migration appendix please include a section on secrets & KMS: when moving from Dedicated to Private ensure customer KMS keys are re-wrapped and update `kms_key_id` in the private config. Also add a checklist item for cert rotation when moving to on-prem.

samir: Also propose a small YAML example for autoscale policy variants, so readers can see latency-driven vs util-driven configs:
```yaml
# latency-driven
autoscale:
  metric: p95_latency_ms
  target: 150
  min: 1
  max: 12
# util-driven
autoscale:
  metric: gpu_utilization_pct
  target: 75
  min: 0
  max: 8
```

devops-bot: CI checks started for PR 4991: spellcheck , link-check , table-lint . See https://ci.redwood.tools/4991/jobs/3

docs-bot: Link-check failed: migration appendix references internal runbook (internal/redwood/private-migration) that needs public-friendly summary or a gated note. Table-lint passed.

leigh: Good catch. We'll add a public summary and a "for enterprise / gated steps" callout that links to the internal runbook. Priya, can you add the callout?

priya: Yep, adding a short callout block: "Enterprise customers should consult their CSM for the gated steps; see internal runbook for HSM/KMS transfer details."

samir: QA note: add an explicit example for drain + reassign in the migration recipe so SREs can test it. CLI example:
```bash
redwoodctl pool drain --pool=team-b --timeout=600
redwoodctl tenant assign --tenant=tenant42 --pool=team-b-new
```

leigh: Also want a tiny section explaining billing implications when moving tenants between pools (reserved vs metered). Priya / Tomas: please add one sentence with a pointer to billing FAQ.

priya: Added billing note pointing to /billing/dedicated-migration with a short example: "moving from reserved 4-GPU to metered reduces monthly commit; estimate costs with the cost calculator."

devops-bot: CI now green for docs lint, but there's one remaining warning in the private migration callout about exposed internal path.

docs-bot: Created follow-up ticket: DOCS-721 to surface the internal steps in a customer-safe way.

leigh: Plan: merge the public pieces first (isolation page, autoscale examples, Go snippet) and put gated steps behind the callout. Aim to merge by Tue COB. Tomas, Samir: can you both review by Monday noon?

tomas: I'm on it, will review and add a tiny note about cert TTL defaults.

samir: I'll review the eviction wording and add the timeline diagram (SVG) as a separate assets PR if needed.

leigh: Thanks all thumbsup: ping here when reviews are in.

priya: ack :thumbsup:

tomas: ack :thumbsup:

samir: ack :thumbsup:
